style: Established Mars expedition illustration: finite compact original equipment, plain local iron bodies, minimal ceramic supports, cleared ground and no decorative hardware. The live design brief owns physical and narrative intent.

goals.text: Restore power to the air scrubber
Carry clean water back to the hab
Give the tent a smooth brick floor
Build and prepare the growing beds
Plant the crops and cover the potato medium
Make a lined basket for the harvest
Clear the filter and restore filling
Take an unmelted reference from the water source
Store it before the farther expedition
Anchor the winch above the loose ramp
Bring the rover to the ice band
Bring back ice from within the band
Make usable iron from local minerals
Build and feed a water-splitting cell
Collect the gases in separate cylinders
Build and connect the methane plant
Wipe the panels and restore power
Block the frame and lay its footing
Cook the soybeans with the potatoes
Secure the core and slab on flight cooling
Fit the arming plug and launch

items.name: Examined ice slab
items.depiction:
![The complete outline in the ice section](assets/fixed/discoveries/intact-body-in-ice.png)

Overlapping plates. Paired, jointed limbs. Where the intake sample held scattered fragments, this outline stays together within the thin section of ice.

I leave the focus there for a long time.

I cannot tell how old it is, or where it came from. But I can send Earth the body and the layer around it together, instead of a handful of broken flakes.

I record the view. Then the slab joins the source core on laboratory cooling; the first fragments remain sealed in their membrane holder. Those three specimens are coming with me. The rest of the remote core stays protected in the laboratory.
